=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:401-466; .claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md:63 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: `record_stalls` marks a stall as seen before the pickup successfully files its `ai:permission-prompt` issue, so a transient filing failure prevents the unchanged stall from being retried.
  WHY: The pickup only files entries marked `new: true`, but that flag is false on the next wake after the seen state has been persisted; all reviewers rated this major, with confidence 4 from deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m3, and z-ai_glm-5_2, and confidence 5 from openai_gpt-6-luna and qwen_qwen3_7-plus.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The same run lists every session, whatever its title, that has waited on a permission prompt for more than 20 minutes: the pickup sends one push notification per stall and files it as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue with the session's title and task summary."
  expected_change_site: `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py::record_stalls` and `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: `record_stalls` persists the "seen" set to `reported-stalls.json` as part of computing which stalls are `new` (lines 437-444, 463-464 of the twin); step 3a.4 runs `permission_prompts.py file --log-dir <stall_log_dir>` only when a stall is `new: true`; the existing test `test_a_stall_is_new_once_and_filed_as_a_permission_prompt_record` covers the happy path but does not assert that a filing failure leaves the stall eligible for retry.
- requirement: “On every hourly wake it also archives the automation sessions whose work is finished and reports sessions stuck on a permission prompt.”
  expected_change_site: `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md`, the queue-read failure path before step 3a
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: The procedure says a failed queue read ends the turn; step 3a, which runs the janitor, comes afterward. Thus a wake with that read failure does not run the janitor or report prompt stalls.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- .claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py:440-449 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Stalls are marked as `new: false` inside `record_stalls` before the pickup calls `permission_prompts.py file`, and a transient failure means the pickup will not call it on the next hourly wake unless a different session is newly stalled.
  WHY: The stall filing is silently dropped, while the operator has already received a notification with no corresponding issue.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

(No findings reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`: `record_stalls` (lines 401-466); consumed by `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script persists each new stall to `<stall-log-dir>/reported-stalls.json` before the pickup files the issue, so transient filing failures silently drop the stall.
  WHY: On the next hourly wake, `record_stalls` finds the same `id@updated_at` in `seen`, sets `stall["new"] = False`, and the pickup skips both the `PushNotification` and `permission_prompts.py file`.
- `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`: `record_stalls` (lines 401-466), paired with `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The pickup cannot detect or retry a filing failure because `record_stalls` exits 0 and no filing failure is mapped back onto the seen ledger.
  WHY: A transient filing failure leaves the stall recorded-but-unfiled, and the next wake will not retry it.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The same run lists every session, whatever its title, that has waited on a permission prompt for more than 20 minutes: the pickup sends one push notification per stall and files it as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue with the session's title and task summary." (PR Description, "Summary"; changelog.d/4648-claude-fixer-session-janitor.md, "Lead paragraph")
  Expected change site: The state-update contract between `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py::record_stalls` and `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4, plus a contract test in `tests/test_stale_sessions.py`.
  Evidence of absence: `record_stalls` persists the "seen" set to `reported-stalls.json` as part of computing which stalls are `new` (lines 437-444, 463-464 of the twin). Step 3a.4 runs `permission_prompts.py file --log-dir <stall_log_dir>` only when a stall is `new: true`. No retry or backfill path exists for filing failures. The existing test `test_a_stall_is_new_once_and_filed_as_a_permission_prompt_record` covers the happy path (two runs, second run sees `new: false`) but does not assert the contract that a filing failure leaves the stall eligible for retry. The plan's "filed as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue" is not guaranteed when the filing step is the one that fails.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`; `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: A stall is recorded as seen before its permission-prompt issue is successfully filed.
  WHY: If `permission_prompts.py` encounters a transient filing error, the next wake marks that stall `new: false` and skips filing it; the issue and notification are not retried while the stall’s `updated_at` remains unchanged.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: “On every hourly wake it also archives the automation sessions whose work is finished and reports sessions stuck on a permission prompt.”
  Expected change site: `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md`, the queue-read failure path before step 3a.
  Evidence of absence: The procedure says a failed queue read ends the turn; step 3a, which runs the janitor, comes afterward. Thus a wake with that read failure does not run the janitor or report prompt stalls.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`: `record_stalls` function, lines 431-466; `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4 | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Stalls are marked as seen in `reported-stalls.json` before the pickup sends the `PushNotification` and runs `permission_prompts.py file` to file the issue.
  WHY: If issue filing fails transiently, the next hourly wake marks it `new: false`, skips filing, and never retries the issue.

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py` (and `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py` twin); `record_stalls`, lines 431-466 (the seen-state write at line 466); `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` step 3a.4 (line 63) | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `record_stalls` persists the seen state and stall records before the pickup attempts to file the stall as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue.
  WHY: If filing fails, the same `id@updated_at` key reads `new: false` on the next hourly wake, so the pickup never retries issue creation.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
